highlights.title: OpenAI and Microsoft knew they were starting a ‘doom loop’ for the web
highlights.summary: Recently unsealed court documents in the New York Times ' case against OpenAI and Microsoft are pretty damning. The companies' own documentation warned that it was starting a "doom loop" that would damage the web, characterized its scraping of data to train its models as the "largest theft of labor…
body: The companies knew they were driving us toward Google Zero, and did it anyway.

Many of the most eye-catching quotes from the document come from Microsoft’s Director of Applied Science, Brent Hecht. Though, the company has tried to distance itself from Hecht’s assertions. Microsoft spokesperson Alex Haurek told The Verge that “These comments reflect one employee’s individual perspective, are not a legal analysis, and do not represent the company’s views.”

In a separate court filing, Jordan Usdan, GM for Data Strategy and Ops at Microsoft AI, characterized Hecht’s role as adversarial. He said that Hecht “holds divergent, academic, and forward-looking views about how data ecosystems for AI should operate and is employed at Microsoft to bring asymmetrical, futuristic, and academic points of view … nor is he someone who speaks for Microsoft specifically as to his theoretical views on AI’s potential effect on content creators.”
But whether or not Microsoft wants to own these comments, it’s clear that this came true. Google Zero is real! AI is eating the web!

highlights.title: Here’s How an AI Slowdown Could Actually Be Enforced
highlights.summary: Even if big AI companies agree to a pause, ensuring that nobody tries to sneak ahead could prove tricky.
body: Many AI researchers seem to firmly believe that the technology they are developing could someday prove very dangerous. What’s less clear—even among AI’s technical elite —is precisely how to keep these mercurial algorithms in check.

In recent years researchers have thrown around all sorts of ideas for preventing AI from turning nasty. They include less controversial plans such as tighter government regulations, new ways of measuring progress, and probing the inner workings of models, as well as more outlandish proposals like placing tracking devices inside GPUs, and even ceremonially destroying large numbers of AI chips.
With political and public pressure now growing for a more measured approach to building AI, however, the answer to keeping AI safe is still unclear.

“We need to start treating this as a research problem,” says Raymond Douglas, an AI researcher at the University of Toronto and coauthor of a new report titled Pacing the Frontier, A Research Agenda, which warns that slowing down AI development remains an unsolved puzzle. “We don't really understand what our options even are or what they will do.”

highlights.title: Should you skip the War Arc (Act 2) in Fire Emblem: Fortune's Weave?
highlights.summary: You can skip the War Arc in Fire Emblem: Fortune's Weave, but while it's not necessarily the best choice, it's not a terrible one either. Whether it's the right one for you depends on where you're at in the game and what you're hoping to get from this part of it.
body: Below, we explain whether you should skip the War Arc in Fire Emblem: Fortune's Weave.

If this is your first time playing through Fortune's Weave, then no, you absolutely should not skip the War Arc at the obelisk. It's an essential bridge connecting the end of the Flame Lords' first acts to Act 3. It's important even if you aren't interested in the story, too, since it gets you ready to face the much steeper challenges Act 3 throws at you. The battles become bigger and more demanding from here on out.

After that, it depends on what you're doing. The maps and story in Act 2 are the same for every character, except for a unique scene at the start and very end. You aren't missing anything there if you skip.

highlights.title: Werner Herzog Picks Up San Sebastian’s Donostia Award at Politically Charged Opening Ceremony
highlights.summary: The evening's hosts, Fariba Sheikhan and Mariona Terés, kicked off the proceedings by condemning the Israel-Gaza war and declaring support for 'NAZA' directors Yuval Abraham and Rachel Szor.
body: German director, screenwriter and producer Werner Herzog touched on the Pyrenees and poetry as he picked up San Sebastian Film Festival ‘s most prestigious honor Friday night in what was a politically charged opening ceremony.
Herzog was recognized with the coveted Donostia Award at the Kursaal Theatre in northern Spain, with a raucous standing ovation from his fellow European creatives.

“I’m here standing in front of you, not as a foreigner,” he continued. “I’ve had a connection to you, the Basque people, through an early film of mine — [1972’s] Aguirre, the Wrath of God,” said Herzog, explaining that he traveled — on foot — “many, many years ago” from the Cannes Film Festival up into the Pyrenees mountain range. It was more than 1,000 kilometers, said the director. “But I must confess, I ended up in Biarritz,” he laughed, “not San Sebastian.”

highlights.title: Gavin Newsom is pushing for an AI kill switch
highlights.summary: California Gov. Gavin Newsom (D) is positioning the state to take the lead on AI oversight, including the potential to mandate a "kill switch" for frontier models, with a new executive order issued Friday.
body: With Congress unlikely to act before the midterms, California is angling to take the lead.

There’s been a flurry of bill discussions in Congress in the wake of former Anthropic researcher Jacob Coxon’s post warning of a more than 10 percent chance that AI “could kill all humans” within a decade. But there’s little hope in Washington that a bill of substance could pass anytime soon given that the House is on recess until November, and the impending midterm elections make major legislation movement in the Senate similarly unlikely. At the same time, President Donald Trump has insisted, “The only control or ‘guardrails’ that AI needs is a STRONG AND ​SMART (High IQ!) PRESIDENT, and the U.S.A. has that, in spades!”

highlights.title: Arteta: Dowman could go out on loan in future
highlights.summary: Arsenal manager Mikel Arteta has not ruled out loaning out Max Dowman in the future and says the club evaluates the 16-year-old sensation's progress every six months.
body: Dowman continued his rise by starting and scoring twice in Arsenal's Carabao Cup win over Ipswich this week. After the game, Gunners midfielder Mikel Merino compared the young teenager to Barcelona and Spain star Lamine Yamal.
But those 90 minutes at Portman Road have been Dowman's only minutes of the season, and he did not make Arsenal's matchday squad in the wins over Aston Villa and Sunderland.
"We haven't really listened to any of the [loan] possibilities because we were clear that we want to have him in the squad, that we wanted him to be part of the pre-season," Arteta said.
"I'm going to start to see where we are from there. We will evaluate every six months where we are, what is the best thing for him to do and from there make the right decisions.

highlights.title: Where to find wonder leaves in Fire Emblem Fortune's Weave
highlights.summary: Wonder leaves are common materials you can find in Fire Emblem: Fortune's Weave. You need one of these plants to complete one of Leda's perform quests called "Elegant Drink Recipes." To collect plants in the game, you need to visit specific nodes on the world map and use the command "Search," but…
body: If you need help locating this material, here's where you can find wonder leaves in Fire Emblem: Fortune's Weave.

The only place where you can find wonder leaves is in the Mahapira Garden node in Ogmios region, on the extreme south part of the map. After you have opened the map and reached Theodora's hometown, Megaira, keep going east. Pass the Grania Stronghold and keep heading east until you reach the Fort Zanbar node. From there, go north, heading to the further tip of the shore to find the Mahapira Garden.

The fastest way to get to the Ogmios region is by using the carriage and traveling to the Salacia Posthouse. Your second option, in case you have unlocked Theodora's ships, is to sail south, but this method requires too many turns, and it's only reasonable if you have many days to spare in a chapter. Besides, Ogmios is a late game area, and you should be around level 35 to explore it while in Part 1 of the game.

highlights.title: The Rules These Horror Power Producers Swear by
highlights.summary: Spooky Pictures' Roy Lee and Steven Schneider, and frequent partner Ben Ross of Image Nation look at the deals — and the philosophy — that helps them land project after project.
body: If you’re a producer in the competitive horror landscape, a piece of advice: get an early look at every hot script you can.

That’s one of the trade secrets of Spooky Pictures partners Roy Lee and Steven Schneider, who leverage their relationships to get scripts like Damien McCarthy’s Hokum “a minute early,” as Schneider says.

Released by Neon, Hokum film ended up grossing $25 million on a $5 million budget, and is one of three movies Spooky and Image Nation teamed up to release this year, including two fall festival entries: Casey Affleck’s The Company at Venice and Guy Nattiv’s The Liberation at Telluride and the Toronto International Film Festival, which wraps up this week.
Lee, Schneider and Ross don’t land every script they want, but the percentage is high.

highlights.title: Spot the conversation hogger – and do something about it | Letter
highlights.summary: Penelope Mavor suggests that listening is not a passive act, so you could interrupt the flow. These conversational hoggers … don’t they know we were born with two ears and one mouth for a reason?
body: It is an interesting reflection to see which of the five hoggers more frequently turn up in our own lives. As a people pleaser and introvert, I have a track record of meeting many monologuists. I pretend to listen, but secretly resent them and their audacity. I just want them to ask about me.

I have learned that although interruption can feel violent, sometimes it is a courageous act. When the speaker has just lost connection with the audience and themselves, we have to bring them back. That is what I loved most about the article – it reminded us that we do have options. We can start noticing how we turn up. How am I listening and speaking? What is my responsibility here?
A great listener can help to transform the conversation – listening is not a passive act. And in talking, am I actually being interesting? Am I talking as if being listened to?

highlights.title: FAA tees up $875M AI tool to help manage air traffic congestion
highlights.summary: An AI tool is set to start advising air traffic controllers on managing air traffic in the congested airspace above the Washington, DC, area. The expected launch would be the first step toward a planned nationwide rollout covering the 29 million square miles of US national airspace overseen by the…
body: The FAA describes the SMART system as using AI models to predict air traffic flows and identify potential conflicts based on operational factors like airline schedules, weather, airport capacity, and airspace conditions. US government and industry officials told The Wall Street Journal that SMART could debut for the three major airports in the Washington, DC, area as soon as Monday, September 21.

The decision to launch SMART in a limited scope before going nationwide is the “right call,” said Philip Mann, principal consultant at Vector Strategic Consulting LLC, where he advises on aviation safety and AI governance. Mann previously worked at the FAA in multiple roles for 17 years.

“SMART’s risk was never any single prediction—it is a national-scale system with AI components carrying more unknowns than anything the FAA has fielded,” Mann wrote in an email to Ars. “Every cut in scope shrinks the unknowns.”

highlights.title: What Hollywood thinks about existential AI warnings
highlights.summary: As the tech sector sounds alarms about AI's potential to destroy humanity, entertainment labor groups are urging the public to stay focused on what's already happening.
body: The studios have been silent, but Hollywood’s biggest labor unions aren’t buying the AI apocalypse narrative.

The AI tools used in entertainment production differ from the AI systems that have sparked a recent round of whistleblowing and apocalyptic declarations. They do not seem to be as existentially dangerous as the AI systems that drove former Anthropic researcher Jacob Coxon to quit his job and prompted Anthropic alignment lead Evan Hubinger to insist that the technology could “kill all humans” at some point “within the next decade.”

When I recently spoke with the Screen Actors Guild – American Federation of Television and Radio Artists’ (SAG-AFTRA) chief negotiator Duncan Crabtree Ireland, he told me that the union recognized early on how AI could impact its members’ livelihoods. Most people might not have been familiar with the idea of studios completely replacing human actors with digital replicas, but SAG-AFTRA understood that it had an opportunity to shape public opinion about AI in Hollywood by “ speaking out about it at the earliest possible point we could.”

highlights.title: Classes and unlock requirements in Fire Emblem Fortune's Weave
highlights.summary: Fire Emblem: Fortune's Weave classes work a bit differently than you might be used to if you played Three Houses. They come in several tiers, similar to Three Houses, but some of the intermediate classes only unlock if you meet certain conditions.
body: Below, we list Fire Emblem: Fortune's Weave 's classes and how to unlock them. This is an in-progress guide, as we're still missing a few master-tier and divine-tier classes. However, those are unavailable until Act 3, so you won't have to do anything to get them until then.

Every character starts in a beginner class, either commoner or noble, and gets a helpful little class mastery skill. After that, it's time to change to something more specialized. A new tier of classes unlocks when you reach certain renown thresholds, and you'll need to purchase certifications to take that class' exam. The game autosaves before you see the exam result, so there's no chance of cheesing it and retaking the exam until you pass.

The better option is to just hold off taking an exam until your character has at least a 75% chance of passing or higher. Skill rank matters here, but level matters even more. If you need to be level 35, for example, but you take the exam at level 32 with the right skill ranks, you'll still end up with a low chance of passing.

highlights.title: Marks and Spencer’s first LFW catwalk gamble pays off with compelling looks at affordable prices
highlights.summary: Retailer’s message is ‘fashion with a small f’ as it picks up on trends and brings styles for everyone to debut runway show. Joan Collins declared the coats “very chic”, and has her eye on a graceful ivory evening dress with caped shoulders.
body: The show, held at the Design Museum for 310 guests including Ian Wright and Jamie Carragher, was a gamble on both sides. Would snobby fashionistas be traumatised by elasticated waistbands and practical rainwear? Would M&S customers be alienated by a world of £2,000 handbags and shoes you can’t walk in?

The style message was “fashion with a small f, not a capital F”, said the M&S womenswear director, Maddy Evans. The look was new enough to be compelling (sharp kilts instead of flouncy tiered skirts, low-rise slouchy denim replacing mom jeans), but pitched at a before-the-watershed comfort level. A judicious amount of catwalk theatre was added with some sauce (a very short skirt, the odd semi-visible nipple) and a little zeitgeisty styling (faux fur stoles, Charli xcx-adjacent sunglasses).

The real stunner is the price. All the clothes in this collection went on sale as the show began on Friday, with half of the pieces under £50. The most expensive, a leather coat, will retail for £450. The message – that catwalk style is for everyone – is a win for London fashion week, which has struggled to feel relevant to real lives as designer prices have soared during a cost of living crisis.

highlights.summary: As it marks its 10-year anniversary, MIT Reads is being reimagined for the age of artificial intelligence. Recognizing the need to foster social connection and a sense of our shared humanity, the popular MIT Libraries’ program will turn its focus to fiction and memoir, and to the particular power…
body: “At MIT, we spend a great deal of time on imagining and building for the future. Reading fiction prompts us to think about how what we build might change us,” says MIT Libraries Director Chris Bourg. “Reading together also gives us the increasingly rare opportunity for both individual reflection and shared connection.”

MIT Reads is also evolving with MIT as it explores AI’s influence on the education landscape and the social fabric of the Institute. The value of collective reading, reflection, and discussion has never been more relevant.

A recently released report from MIT’s Ad Hoc Committee on AI Use in Teaching, Learning, and Research Training urges strengthening social connection and personal well-being, citing MIT Reads as a way to “engage many more people across campus in conversation about shared norms and why community matters.”

Launched in 2016, MIT Reads was designed to foster empathy, understanding, and belonging within the campus community. Each selected book is accompanied by programming such as talks by the featured author, panel discussions, and small-group conversations facilitated by library staff.

highlights.summary: Developer Rebel Wolves' September success story, The Blood of Dawnwalker, cost just $40 million to make. Information related to the Warsaw, Poland-based studio's behind-the-scenes activities comes from a new Bloomberg report.
body: Game designer Konrad Tomaszkiewicz, who previously served as one of the leading developers behind games like The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt and Cyberpunk 2077, worked on early versions of Rebel Wolves' first game with a small team back in 2022. Tomaszkiewicz self-funded the project for that first year as the team hammered out its prototype in hopes of finding a partner, with NetEase later stepping in with the fund the game while acquiring 26% of the studio.

The $40 million figure comfortably lands The Blood of Dawnwalker in the AA space instead of the AAA realm where games often carry heftier price tags. For comparison, IO Interactive's 007 First Light reportedly carried a budget of more than $200 million. Sony's struggling Marathon game is said to have had a similar budget, with games like The Last of Us Part 2 and Horizon Forbidden West also reportedly in that range.

highlights.title: Why Europe has been absent from the great AI safety debate
highlights.summary: Though Europe has measures that address how consumers might encounter AI, technology will impact them if the worst scenarios bear. Europe’s dilemma over AI was rendered in stark terms this week.
body: The great debate over AI safety that has erupted in recent days threatens to make the choice moot. If the worst scenarios come to bear – and experts have differing views on this – then the technology will impact the continent regardless.

Europe has largely been absent from the highest levels of that debate, a result of the continent’s longstanding inability to produce a Silicon Valley-scale titan like Apple, Google or newcomer OpenAI. While it is a powerhouse in regulation, much to the White House’s chagrin, its lack of an Anthropic or Nvidia-sized frontrunner in the AI race has diminished its voice in the safety debate.

Ursula von der Leyen, a powerful political figure on the continent as president of the European Commission, the EU’s executive arm, addressed the issue this week by saying she will “invite the main frontier labs for a discussion on how we can support ongoing industry efforts to pace the frontier”.

Her remarks gained nowhere as much traction as Donald Trump and China’s dismissal of a slowdown. Without the support of Washington or Beijing, any sort of pacing is impossible – with our without Europe’s input.

highlights.title: AI PACs Have Dumped Nearly $1 Million Into an Obscure Senate Race
highlights.summary: The reliably Republican South Dakota senate seat has an incumbent on the ballot. But PACs associated with AI labs and investors have already spent more money on the race than actual residents have.
body: Major super PACs associated with AI labs and investors have poured close to $1 million into incumbent Republican Mike Rounds’s South Dakota senate race, seeking to shape the outcome of a noncompetitive race amid a critical national debate over AI regulation.

Rounds has been the beneficiary this cycle of around $600,000 in spending by outside groups, with the vast majority of that figure coming from the super PAC Defend American Jobs, which receives funding from a super PAC financed by the venture capital firm Andreessen Horowitz.

He has also received roughly $215,000 directly from the employees and super PACs affiliated with AI labs, most notably Anthropic, as well as a constellation of other tech companies including Google and Microsoft, according to FEC filings.

With fewer than 50 days until the midterm elections in November, recent polls show Rounds ahead of the independent candidate Brian Beng after the Democratic candidate Julian Beaudion dropped out last month.

highlights.title: Fire Emblem: Fortune's Weave Is Way Easier If You Play a Second Route
highlights.summary: Fire Emblem: Fortune's Weave lets you clear the whole game by playing just one route — or none at all if you're a real sicko and ignore the Flame Lords. But you really, really should do at least two routes before tackling the final campaign against Balor.
body: And you shouldn't start it until you finish at least one extra route.
In short, yes, you should definitely play a second route in Fire Emblem: Fortune’s Weave.

Whoever you pick first, you'll be up against it in terms of money, renown, and balancing free time with exploring the map to find better weapons and gifts. Some characters can get more money or renown than others thanks to their unique subquests, but regardless, the number of quests in each chapter is limited. Every character has a handful of potential allies they can recruit at a lower level of renown, but "handful" is the operative word there. The rest require a renown level of seven or higher.

Act 2 expands the number of characters you can deploy in each mission to 15. It does supply a few of them if you don't have enough, but these are guest units, and as such, you have no control over their equipment and class. And sure, you can go up against the seemingly endless horde of foes that act throws at you, though having 12 to 15 characters makes managing the pressure much easier.
points: Fire Emblem: Fortune's Weave lets you clear the whole game by playing just one route — or none at all if you're a real sicko and ignore the Flame Lords.

highlights.summary: Virginia Gov. Abigail Spanberger ordered the state government to take steps that could empower local communities to have a larger say in data center development and slow down approvals in a state that is already home to the data center capital of the world.
body: Democratic Gov. Abigail Spanberger signed an executive order addressing data centers and AI risks.

Executive Order 22 bans executive branch officials from signing nondisclosure agreements for data center projects, requires expedited noise regulations, and requires a review of backup-generation operations used by data centers, among other requirements. The order also establishes an AI task force responsible for evaluating how the state government can address risks to Virginians like workforce displacement and data privacy issues, and determining how existing law can be applied to AI harms.

The order represents the latest signal that states are taking data center and AI policy into their own hands as Congress and President Donald Trump have been slow or resistant to sweeping changes. Also on Friday, California Gov. Gavin Newsom issued an executive order convening experts to tackle AI safety issues, and earlier, New York Gov. Kathy Hochul and Texas Gov. Greg Abbott have both taken executive action to rein in rapid data center development.

highlights.title: If the AI Industry Followed Its Own Research, It Might Have Paused Already
highlights.summary: Anthropic’s CEO says that safety hinges on understanding how AI “thinks.” So far the evidence is disturbing.
body: In early 2025 I was interviewing Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei when he explained why, despite the company’s repeated acknowledgments that AI could yield catastrophic results, people seemed largely unperturbed. “There is compelling evidence that the models can wreak havoc,” he said. But, he added, those dangers were still theoretical. Would it take a Pearl Harbor–like situation for the world to wake up to those dire possibilities? He sighed. “Basically, yeah,” he said.

As it turned out, all it took was a well-timed X post from one of Amodei’s junior employees to accelerate AI fears to the top of the global agenda. On September 8, Jacob Coxon publicly posted his resignation, charging that Anthropic and other frontier AI companies were “racing straight to self-improving intelligence and gambling with our lives.” Almost instantly a more senior Anthropic engineer confirmed that many within the company thought that their work had a 10 percent chance of wiping out humanity.

highlights.summary: Those early season thoughts that Chelsea might be the team best placed to challenge Arsenal are beginning to look over-optimistic. The two chaotic wins with which they began the season were always difficult to read: they might have been useful points picked up on the way to a more solid structure…
body: Brentford’s first home win over Chelsea since 1938 means they remain unbeaten, third in the table, coherent and disciplined. The comparison is impossible not to draw: as one side flails in an orgy of structured spending, their far less wealthy neighbours thrive with a clear plan and sense of direction.

Such is the state of perpetual flux at Chelsea that the usual homilies about the benefits of stability always seem a little redundant when applied to them. With 11 new signings this summer maintaining the sense of the club as a trading hub, learning the names of everybody in the dressing room has probably been a greater priority than worrying too much about boardroom wrangling but, still, their first game since Todd Boehly and Mark Walter agreed to sell their 12.8% stakes in the club to the major shareholder Clearlake Capital felt significant. At the very least, a more harmonious boardroom should be beneficial.

body: Like any popular anime series, however, Witch Hat Atelier got its start as a really popular manga series. The art style of Kamome Shirahama is absolutely stunning and blends classic manga techniques with modern comic book illustration. If you've never read manga before, this is a great place to start. And with the most recent discount at Amazon, now is a good time to snag the first six volumes for cheap.

The first Witch Hat Atelier box set includes the first six volumes, which is only a portion of the ongoing series. There are currently only 14 volumes available in English, so this set collects almost half of what's available right now.

For those who have already seen the anime, you should already be familiar with the content of the first four volumes. Episode 13 concluded the first season by adapting the story up through the end of volume 4, meaning volumes 5 and 6 will continue the story where the show left off. Like any adaptation, there are plenty of extras you'll get to experience by reading the manga that wasn't shown in the anime.
